body:
This adds a mode to the unittester that turns DuckDB warnings into errors, plus a CI config run that uses it. Tests can then no longer quietly rely on deprecated behavior such as the no-op `PRAGMA enable_verification`.

### The mode
- New test config option `warnings_as_errors` (also available as `--warnings-as-errors` / `--no-warnings-as-errors`). With it on, the runner sets `logging_level='WARNING'`, `enable_logging=true` and `warnings_as_errors=true` on every database it creates. That uses the existing `warnings_as_errors` setting, so a statement that logs a warning fails with the warning as its error:
  ```
  Query unexpectedly failed! (test/...:4)!
  PRAGMA enable_verification;
  Invalid Input Error: The 'enable_verification' pragma no longer has any effect; it is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
  ```
- `test/configs/warnings_as_errors.json` runs the suite in this mode. It is added to `TEST_CONFIGS_QUERY_VERIFICATION`, so it runs in the "Linux Config (Query Verification)" CI job.
- AGENTS.md now mentions the rule.

### Cleanups so the config passes
- Removed the no-op `PRAGMA enable/disable_verification` and `enable/disable_object_cache` from 60 tests, along with comments that explained them.
- Rewrote `PRAGMA name=value` to `SET name=value` in 796 tests. This is a mechanical change in its own commit. Bare identifier values are quoted, because `SET explain_output=all` does not parse while the PRAGMA form converted identifiers to strings. Malformed PRAGMA lines that test parser errors are left as they are. `pragma_assignment_deprecated.test` still covers the deprecated form.
- Replaced implicit identifier-to-string conversions in about 20 tests with string literals: bare type names in `columns=` / `hive_types=` / `dtypes=`, double-quoted file paths, `format = auto`, and similar. `SHOW t` / `SHOW (query)` are now `DESCRIBE`, and an unordered `OFFSET` now has `ORDER BY rowid`.

### Engine fixes found by the new config
- **COPY `PARTITION_BY` warned for JSON/GeoJSON.** Formats that do not register `copy_options` skipped the generic COPY option list, so `PARTITION_BY (part)` with a bare column was treated as a deprecated identifier conversion. Parquet was already exempt and tested. Added `test/sql/json/copy_json_partition_by_identifier.test`.
- **`CALL enable_logging()` always warned that CLI warnings may be lost**, even when it kept the shell's log storage or the shell was not involved at all. It now warns only when it moves logging away from `shell_log_storage`. A shell test covers the no-warning case.

### Skipped in this config (132 tests, grouped by reason in the JSON)
- Tests that check a warning on purpose, or the behavior with `warnings_as_errors` off.
- Logging tests that rely on the default logging configuration, which this config changes.
- Tests of deprecated settings: `lambda_syntax` (35), `profiling_mode` (12), `delim_join_as_cte`, `error_on_division_by_zero`, `*_metadata_reuse`, `old_implicit_casting`, `legacy_*`, and `extension_directory` (9, which could migrate to `extension_directories` in a follow-up).
- Views stored by older versions with the lambda arrow syntax.
- Tests whose queries apply `OFFSET` to an unordered input.
- **Possible false positive, needs a decision:** table macros such as `histogram_values(tbl, col)`, `compute_top_k(...)` and `query_table(tbl)` take table and column names as bare identifiers, which the identifier-conversion deprecation warns about. Following the warning's advice changes the result: `histogram_values('integers', 'i')` bins the constant string `'i'` instead of column `i`. These 9 tests are skipped instead of "fixed". The deprecation probably needs to exempt table-macro parameters.

### Testing
- `build/reldebug/test/run --test-config test/configs/warnings_as_errors.json`: 6123 passed, 0 failed (77 skipped by `require`/`require-env`)
- `build/reldebug/test/run` (default, no config) after the rewrite: 8824 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `Test path canonicalization with symlinks`, which fails only because I pointed `--temp-dir-root` at `/dev/shm` on the shared box; it passes with the default temp dir
- Slow tests touched by the PRAGMA→SET rewrite: all 185 touched `.test_slow` files run: 179 passed, 6 skipped by `require`
- Shell (`tools/shell/tests/test_warning.py`): pytest isn't installed on the box I used, so I checked the two cases by hand with the CLI. `CALL enable_logging(level='warning')` followed by `CALL enable_logging(level='info', storage='shell_log_storage')` prints no warning, and switching to `storage='file'` still prints it.
- `make format-fix` was not run (no clang-format/black available on that box). The C++ and Python edits are small and follow the surrounding style; the Code Quality check will catch anything off.

review_comments.body:
The CLI now silently loses warnings for some logging changes. A higher level or log type filter keeps `shell_log_storage`, so this check skips the notice even though later warnings no longer reach it. On the base, every call printed the notice. Could we also warn when the new configuration stops logging `WARNING` entries, for example with a level above `WARNING` or an enabled log type list?

```sql
CALL enable_logging(level = 'error');
-- base: WARNING: The logging settings have been changed so you may lose warnings printed in the CLI.
-- head: no notice
PRAGMA enable_verification;
-- base and head: its deprecation warning is no longer printed
```

The same happens with `CALL enable_logging('QueryLog');`.

These table-macro tests do not need to be skipped. The warning concerns only the table name: quoting it while keeping the column as an identifier preserves the result without a warning. Quoting the column too makes it a constant string. `test/sql/aggregate/aggregates/histogram_table_function.test` passes under this config with only the table names quoted in `histogram_values` and `histogram`, and fails unchanged. I would fix those calls and remove the skip; the deprecation probably needs no exemption for table-macro parameters.

```sql
SELECT * FROM histogram_values('integers', i, bin_count := 2);
-- 60 1, 80 0, 100 1, no warning
SELECT * FROM histogram_values('integers', 'i', bin_count := 2);
-- i 2: the column becomes a constant string
```

This assertion can pass even when the statement fails, because it only checks that the text is absent from stdout. That can hide a failure unrelated to the notice. I would use the existing `check_not_exist` helper, which also checks the exit status; this replacement passes on the head.

```suggestion
    result.check_not_exist("The logging settings have been changed")
```

New parametrized shell test `test_dropping_warnings_from_shell_log_storage_warns` covers `enable_logging(level = 'error')` and `enable_logging('QueryLog')`. It fails without the change, and `test_keeping_shell_log_storage_does_not_warn` still passes.

Done in 2d96a34d3ba: the table-macro skip is removed. All nine tests now quote only the table names (e.g. `histogram_values('integers', i, ...)`, `compute_top_k('lineitem', ...)`, `query_table(['tbl', 'tbl2'])`). Each test passes with and without `--test-config test/configs/warnings_as_errors.json` with the same assertion counts. `arg_min_max_n_tpch.test` needs tpch, so I couldn't run it here.
